entries.meaning: To do a job, especially one you are paid for. ---
examples: I work for a small firm downtown.
She worked late three nights in a row.
He has been working here since 2019.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (work long hours), intransitive (she works downtown)
entries.contrast: Work FOR a company, work AT a place, work ON a project, work WITH people. The preposition changes the meaning, not the verb.

entries.meaning: To pay someone to work for you. ---
examples: The plant employs about two hundred people.
They employed him as a night manager.
She has been employed by the same firm for ten years.
entries.contrast: The -y follows a vowel, so nothing changes: employs, employed. Compare carry - carries - carried.

entries.meaning: To give someone a job. ---
examples: We hire new engineers every spring.
They hired her on the spot.
The company is hiring two more designers.
entries.contrast: Drop the -e before -ing: hiring, not hireing. Hire sounds exactly like higher.

entries.meaning: To find and bring in new people to work for an organization. ---
examples: Big banks recruit heavily on college campuses.
We recruited four analysts last quarter.
They are recruiting for a new sales team.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (recruit engineers), intransitive (we are recruiting again)

entries.meaning: To teach someone the skills a job needs. ---
examples: We train every new hire for two weeks.
She trained as an accountant before switching to law.
He has trained most of the staff on the new system.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (train new hires), intransitive (he trained as a nurse)

entries.meaning: To be in charge of a business, a team, or a difficult situation. ---
examples: She manages a team of twelve.
He managed the store for eight years.
Who is managing the project while you are away?
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (manage a team), intransitive (somehow we managed)

entries.meaning: To watch over people or work and make sure it is done properly. ---
examples: Two engineers supervise the night shift.
She supervised the move to the new office.
The interns are supervised by a senior developer.

entries.meaning: To move someone into a higher position, or to help a product become better known. ---
examples: Good managers promote from within.
They promoted her to regional director.
He has been promoted twice in three years.

entries.meaning: To officially leave a job or position. ---
examples: Two board members resign every year by rotation.
He resigned after the merger was announced.
She is resigning at the end of the month.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (resign his post), intransitive (she resigned in May)
entries.contrast: The g is silent: ri-ZYN. You resign FROM a company. Re-sign, meaning to sign again, is a different word: ree-SYN.

entries.meaning: To make someone leave their job, usually for poor work or bad behavior. ---
examples: No boss enjoys having to fire anyone.
They fired him for missing three deadlines.
Two people were fired after the audit.
entries.contrast: Drop the -e before -ing: firing. Fire is blunt; let go and dismiss are the polite versions.

entries.meaning: To put a new person or thing in the place of another. ---
examples: We replace the laptops every four years.
She replaced the retiring director in June.
Who is replacing him while he is on leave?
entries.contrast: Replace X WITH Y, not replace X on Y.

entries.meaning: To get money for work you do, or to deserve something through effort. ---
examples: Engineers here earn well above the average.
She earned a bonus for closing the deal.
He has earned the trust of the whole team.

entries.meaning: To plan and arrange something, or to put things in order. ---
examples: She organizes the annual sales meeting.
They organized the files by client.
We are organizing a training day for June.
entries.contrast: American spelling -ize: organize, organized. British writing uses -ise: organise, organised.

entries.meaning: To make the plans that are needed for something to happen. ---
examples: I will arrange a call for Thursday.
She arranged the whole trip in one afternoon.
Transportation has already been arranged.

entries.meaning: To make different people or parts of a job work together smoothly. ---
examples: She coordinates the work of four teams.
We coordinated the launch with the marketing department.
He is coordinating the move to the new building.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (coordinate the launch), intransitive (coordinate with the vendor)

entries.meaning: To give part of your work or authority to someone else. ---
examples: Strong managers delegate instead of doing everything themselves.
He delegated the reporting to his assistant.
By delegating the paperwork, she freed up two days a week.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (delegate the task), intransitive (good managers delegate)
entries.contrast: The verb ends in -gayt; the noun, a person sent to a conference, ends in a schwa: DEL-uh-guht.

entries.meaning: To give a person a particular job, task, or place. ---
examples: They assign each new hire a mentor.
She assigned the audit to two junior staff.
I have been assigned to the Boston account.
entries.contrast: The g is silent: uh-SYN. Assign a task TO someone.

entries.meaning: To give out money, time, or resources for a particular purpose. ---
examples: The board allocates the budget every October.
They allocated two engineers to the project.
Half the funds have already been allocated.

entries.meaning: To run a business or a machine, or to be active and working. ---
examples: The company operates in twelve countries.
He operated a small repair shop for years.
The plant has been operating at half capacity.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (operate the machinery), intransitive (the firm operates in six states)

entries.meaning: To keep something in good condition or at the same level. ---
examples: We maintain records for seven years.
They maintained production right through the strike.
The equipment is maintained twice a year.

entries.meaning: To change something to a different time. ---
examples: Can we reschedule for Friday?
They rescheduled the interview twice.
The flight was rescheduled for the next morning.

entries.meaning: To move an event or a decision to a later time. ---
examples: Let us not postpone the decision again.
They postponed the launch until spring.
The hearing has been postponed indefinitely.
entries.русский: откладывать, отложить; переносить на более поздний срок

entries.meaning: To make something happen later than planned, or to be slow to act. ---
examples: Bad weather often delays deliveries.
The strike delayed the whole project by a month.
Our flight has been delayed again.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (delay the shipment), intransitive (do not delay)
entries.contrast: The -y follows a vowel, so it stays: delays, delayed. Compare carry - carries - carried.

entries.meaning: To decide that a planned event or arrangement will not happen. ---
examples: They cancel the class if fewer than five people sign up.
She canceled the order an hour later.
Two flights have been canceled this morning.
entries.contrast: American English keeps one l: canceled, canceling. British English doubles it: cancelled. The noun cancellation has two l's everywhere.

entries.meaning: To be the person or organization that holds an event and receives the guests. ---
examples: Our office hosts the regional meeting every fall.
They hosted a dinner for the visiting clients.
She is hosting the webinar on Thursday.

entries.meaning: To arrange in advance to have a room, a seat, or a service. ---
examples: I always book the aisle seat.
She booked the conference room for two hours.
The hotel is fully booked that week.

entries.meaning: To show or explain something formally to a group of people. ---
examples: I present the numbers at every board meeting.
She presented the plan to the client on Tuesday.
He is presenting at the conference next week.
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed on the second syllable, pri-ZENT; the noun and adjective on the first, PREZ-unt.

entries.meaning: To write something down or store it so that it can be used later. ---
examples: We record every call for training.
She recorded the vote in the minutes.
The session was recorded and shared with the team.
entries.contrast: The verb is ri-KORD; the noun is REK-urd, as in a sales record.

entries.meaning: To make something current, or to tell someone the latest news. ---
examples: Please update me before the call.
They updated the forecast after the holidays.
The policy was updated in January.
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed at the end, up-DAYT; the noun at the front, UP-dayt, as in a quick update.

entries.meaning: To find the size, amount, or degree of something. ---
examples: How do you measure success here?
They measured the impact of the ad campaign.
Performance is measured against last year.

entries.meaning: To settle an argument by each side giving up part of what it wants. ---
examples: Neither side wants to compromise.
They compromised on a two-year contract.
By compromising early, we saved a month of argument.
entries.русский: идти на компромисс, договариваться; ставить под угрозу
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (compromise the deal), intransitive (both sides compromised)
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, and the ending sounds like -myz, not -mees.

entries.meaning: To politely refuse something, or to go down in amount or quality. ---
examples: I have to decline the invitation.
Profits declined for three quarters in a row.
She has declined two offers this year.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (decline the invitation), intransitive (sales declined)

entries.meaning: To need something, or to make something a rule. ---
examples: The job requires three years of experience.
They required two forms of identification.
A signature is required on every page.

entries.meaning: To end an argument or a debt by agreement. ---
examples: Most cases like this settle before trial.
They settled the claim out of court.
The invoice has been settled in full.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (settle the dispute), intransitive (the two sides settled)

entries.meaning: To put something into its final, agreed form. ---
examples: We finalize the budget in November.
They finalized the deal on Friday afternoon.
The wording is still being finalized.

entries.meaning: To write a first version of a document. ---
examples: Legal will draft the agreement.
She drafted the email but never sent it.
A new policy is being drafted.
entries.contrast: American /æ/: DRAFT, not DRAHFT.

entries.meaning: To make an agreement, a license, or a subscription valid for another period. ---
examples: We renew the lease every two years.
She renewed her contract for another term.
The license has not been renewed.
entries.contrast: American ri-NOO, not ri-NYOO.

entries.meaning: To make something last longer or reach further. ---
examples: Can you extend the deadline by a week?
They extended his contract through December.
The warranty has been extended to three years.

entries.meaning: To act or to speak officially for a person, a group, or a company. ---
examples: Two lawyers represent the company in court.
She represented us at the trade show.
The union is representing the night shift.

entries.meaning: To give official permission for something. ---
examples: Only two people authorize payments over ten thousand dollars.
She authorized the overtime herself.
The purchase was never authorized.
entries.contrast: American -ize, British -ise: authorize, authorise.

entries.meaning: To allow something officially. ---
examples: The rules do not permit outside contractors on site.
They permitted us to use the loading dock.
Smoking is not permitted anywhere in the building.
entries.contrast: Stress falls on the last syllable, so the t doubles: permitted, permitting. The noun, a document, is stressed at the front: PUR-mit.

entries.meaning: To choose someone officially for a job or a position. ---
examples: The board appoints the chief executive.
They appointed her head of operations.
A new auditor has been appointed.

entries.meaning: To create something over time, or to grow and become more advanced. ---
examples: Our team develops software for hospitals.
They developed the prototype in four months.
We are developing a cheaper version.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (develop a product), intransitive (the market developed quickly)
entries.contrast: No doubled p and no final e: developed, developing, development.

entries.meaning: To plan how something will look or work before it is made. ---
examples: She designs packaging for food brands.
They designed the store layout themselves.
The system was designed for small teams.
entries.contrast: The g is silent: di-ZYN. It comes back in designate and designation.

entries.meaning: To make or grow something, especially in large amounts. ---
examples: The plant produces four thousand units a day.
They produced the entire run in Mexico.
Most of our parts are produced locally.
entries.contrast: The verb is pruh-DOOSS; the noun produce, meaning fruit and vegetables, is PROH-dooss.

entries.meaning: To make goods in a factory, usually in large quantities. ---
examples: They manufacture medical equipment in Ohio.
These chips were manufactured in Taiwan.
The company has been manufacturing here since 1962.

entries.meaning: To advertise and sell a product to a particular group of buyers. ---
examples: They market the service to small businesses.
The drink was marketed as a health product.
We are marketing it mainly through social media.
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t does not double: marketed, marketing.

entries.meaning: To tell the public about a product, a service, or a job. ---
examples: We advertise openings on three job boards.
They advertised the sale for two weeks.
The job was never advertised publicly.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (advertise the position), intransitive (we advertise on the radio)
entries.contrast: Always -ise, in America too: advertise, never advertize. Compare organize and analyze, which do change.

entries.meaning: To provide someone with something they need, especially goods. ---
examples: Two farms supply all of our produce.
They supplied the parts at cost.
The materials are supplied by a local firm.
entries.contrast: Consonant plus -y: supplies, supplied, but supplying keeps the y. Supply someone WITH something.

entries.meaning: To buy something, especially in formal or business language. ---
examples: The city purchases its vehicles through a state contract.
They purchased the building in 2019.
Equipment purchased this year is still under warranty.

entries.meaning: To send someone a statement of how much they owe. ---
examples: We bill clients at the end of the month.
They billed us twice for the same visit.
You will be billed only after delivery.
entries.contrast: Bill someone FOR something: they billed us for the repair.

entries.meaning: To provide the money for a project or an organization. ---
examples: Two investors fund most of the research.
The state funded half the construction.
The program is funded through 2027.

entries.meaning: To plan how much money you will spend on something. ---
examples: We budget about five percent for training.
They budgeted twenty thousand dollars for the move.
Nobody had budgeted for a second audit.
entries.русский: планировать бюджет, закладывать в бюджет; выделять средства
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (budget ten thousand dollars), intransitive (budget for repairs)
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t stays single: budgeted, budgeting. Budget FOR something.

entries.meaning: To become larger, or to make something larger. ---
examples: Small firms expand slowly at first.
They expanded into Canada last year.
We have been expanding the team all spring.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (expand the range), intransitive (the firm expanded)

entries.meaning: To buy or obtain something, especially a company, a property, or a skill. ---
examples: Big platforms acquire small startups every month.
They acquired the rights for two million dollars.
The company was acquired by a German group.

entries.meaning: To start an organization or a system that is meant to last. ---
examples: New owners usually establish their own rules.
They established the firm in a garage.
The company was established in 1948.
entries.contrast: After -sh the third person adds -es: establishes.

entries.meaning: To start a company, a school, or an organization. ---
examples: It takes nerve to found a company alone.
She founded the agency at twenty-six.
The firm was founded by two former teachers.
entries.contrast: This is a regular verb: found - founded - founded. Do not confuse it with found, the past of find. He founded the company; he found the keys.

entries.meaning: To have something as your property. ---
examples: She owns two restaurants downtown.
They owned the building before the bank took it.
The chain is owned by a family in Texas.
entries.contrast: Own describes a state, so it is rarely used in the -ing form: she owns it, not she is owning it.

entries.meaning: To pay to use a property for a period, or to let someone use yours for payment. ---
examples: We rent the second floor.
They rented a warehouse near the airport.
The office has been rented to a law firm.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (rent an office), intransitive (we rent, we do not own)
entries.contrast: Rent FROM the owner, rent TO a tenant. American English uses rent for both sides; the British often say let for the owner's side.

entries.meaning: To make something better, or to become better. ---
examples: Small changes improve the process a lot.
Delivery times improved after the new software.
Service has been improving since January.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (improve the process), intransitive (results improved)

entries.meaning: To become greater in number or amount, or to make something greater. ---
examples: We increase prices once a year.
Sales increased by nine percent.
Rent has increased every year since 2020.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (increase the price), intransitive (costs increased)
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed at the end, in-KREESS; the noun at the front, IN-kreess, as in a pay increase.

entries.meaning: To make something smaller in size, amount, or price. ---
examples: We need to reduce overtime.
They reduced the headcount by twenty.
Costs have been reduced by a third.
entries.contrast: American ri-DOOSS, not ri-DYOOSS.

entries.meaning: To finish something, or to fill in every part of a form. ---
examples: Please complete the form before Friday.
They completed the building two months early.
The training must be completed within thirty days.

entries.meaning: To bring something to an end, or to come to an end. ---
examples: He usually finishes by six.
She finished the report on the train.
We are finishing the last section today.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (finish the report), intransitive (the meeting finished at five)
entries.contrast: Finish DOING something, never finish to do: I finished writing the report.

entries.meaning: To succeed in reaching a goal after effort. ---
examples: Few teams achieve that in a single quarter.
They achieved record sales in December.
Nothing would have been achieved without her.
entries.contrast: Spelled -ie-: achieve, achieved, not acheive.

entries.meaning: To finish something successfully, especially something difficult. ---
examples: Long meetings rarely accomplish much.
The team accomplished a great deal in six weeks.
We have accomplished everything on the list.
entries.contrast: After -sh the third person adds -es: accomplishes.

entries.meaning: To not succeed, or to not do something that you should have done. ---
examples: Most new restaurants fail in the first year.
The supplier failed to deliver on time.
Two of the three pilot projects have failed.
entries.русский: терпеть неудачу, провалиться; не суметь, не справиться
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (fail the exam), intransitive (the business failed)
entries.contrast: Fail TO DO something: he failed to answer, not he failed answering.

entries.meaning: To work for a person, an organization, or a group of customers. ---
examples: One office serves the whole region.
He served as treasurer for six years.
Over a thousand clients are served each month.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (serve customers), intransitive (she served on the board)

entries.meaning: To deal with documents, data, or materials in an official or standard way. ---
examples: The bank processes refunds in five days.
They processed my application the same week.
Your order is being processed.
entries.contrast: American English stresses the first syllable and uses the LOT vowel: PRAH-sess.

entries.meaning: To send an official document to an authority, or to store papers in order. ---
examples: Most companies file their taxes in March.
She filed a complaint with the labor board.
The paperwork was filed a week late.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (file a complaint), intransitive (file for bankruptcy)
entries.contrast: Drop the -e before -ing: filing. File FOR bankruptcy, file a complaint WITH an office.

entries.meaning: To pay an outside company to do work that your own staff used to do. ---
examples: Many firms outsource payroll.
They outsourced customer support to a call center.
Half of our technical work is now outsourced.

entries.meaning: To make a process run by machines or software instead of by people. ---
examples: We automate anything we do more than twice.
They automated the whole billing cycle.
Most of the reporting is now automated.

entries.meaning: To give things out to a number of people, or to supply goods to stores.
examples: Two warehouses distribute to the whole West Coast.
They distributed the agenda before the meeting.
Bonuses are distributed in December.
